misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: Transaction execution is an internal EVM process, not an external entity. The transaction itself comes from external sources, but the execution environment is the EVM's internal machinery processing the transaction.
CREATE is an internal EVM opcode/operation, not an external entity that sends data into the system. Contract deployment originates from external transactions but CREATE itself is internal.
The EVM interpreter is the core internal component executing bytecode. It processes external inputs but is not itself an external entity.

misclassified_entities.original_description: Malicious validator operator attempting testnet takeover
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: An 'attacker' represents adversarial intent within the threat model, not a distinct external entity type. Malicious validators use the same interfaces as legitimate validators. Threat modeling should consider attacker motivations but model them as the same entity type (validator operator) with malicious intent.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Entity that deployed the contract bytecode being analyzed for jump destinations
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any account can deploy contracts with arbitrary bytecode. The deployed code may contain malicious patterns, invalid opcodes, or attempt to exploit jump destination analysis. The EVM correctly treats all deployed bytecode as untrusted and performs thorough jump destination validation.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - any funded account can deploy contracts

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External account or contract initiating a message call that triggers code execution
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any contract or EOA can initiate message calls (CALL, DELEGATECALL, etc.) with arbitrary calldata and target addresses. The caller controls execution flow by providing the target address and input data. Jump destination validation exists specifically because callers are untrusted.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - any account can make calls

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Decentralized application providing EIP-712 typed data structures for signing
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: DApps provide the typed data structures (including box types) that users sign. A malicious DApp could construct misleading typed data that obscures the true nature of what is being signed. The EIP-7713 box type specification exists to improve transparency, but DApp-provided data remains untrusted.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - DApp is untrusted web application

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Wallet application parsing and displaying EIP-712 typed data including box types
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Wallet software is installed by the user, implying trust. However, it acts as the security boundary between DApp-provided data and user decisions. The wallet must correctly parse box types and display contents transparently. Wallets are trusted for UI presentation but must validate all incoming typed data structures.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: User installation and selection of wallet software

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Human user reviewing and signing EIP-712 typed data messages
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: The user is the final decision maker who approves or rejects signatures. Users are trusted to make their own decisions but may be deceived by malicious typed data presentations. Box types help by making nested content visible, but users can still be socially engineered.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Smart contract that will verify the EIP-712 signature and execute based on signed data
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: The contract receiving the signature is untrusted - it could be a malicious contract designed to extract value once a signature is obtained. The domain separator binds signatures to specific contracts, but users must verify they are signing for the intended contract.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - any contract can request EIP-712 signatures

boundary_edges.data_flow_description: Contract deployer submits bytecode that will be analyzed for valid jump destinations
External caller initiates message call that loads target code and begins execution
DApp provides EIP-712 typed data structure including box types for wallet parsing
Wallet software parses box types and displays expanded contents to user for review
User reviews displayed data and approves signature creation

coverage_gaps.reason: No explicit incoming edge - this entity receives signatures produced by the system rather than sending data into it. It defines the domain separator that influences signing but acts as an outbound verification target.

coverage_analysis.notes: EIP-140 REVERT (spec_834c0eab895dcf9616a42e389ac43071bd019772) has no external entities - REVERT is purely internal EVM state rollback. Spurious Dragon (spec_89215af633cb.json) entities were all misclassified internal EVM components. EIP-6916 testnet reset (spec_8c6f1d7d7517.json) attacker is a threat model pattern not an external entity. Cancun memory operations (spec_8f34eb1fd09b.json) has no external entities - MLOAD/MSTORE/MSTORE8/MCOPY/MSIZE are internal EVM memory operations. EIP-7713 box type (spec_9210de6848d07e83d52ba8cd7555e8f05e2889df.json) has significant trust boundary concerns around DApp-provided typed data and user signature approval flows.
